identity.retryPolicy: Transport failures (timeout (180s), network error, HTTP 408/409/429/5xx, unreadable API response with 5xx, incomplete or missing output) are retried up to 4 attempts per turn with exponential backoff honoring Retry-After and provider reset headers. Live calls use a 5-second minimum pace, increasing automatically to stay under 80% of a reported token/minute limit, and live episodes cool down by 30 seconds; every attempt and sanitized rate-limit header is recorded. Exhausted HTTP 429 retries interrupt the batch as infrastructure rather than counting as model failure. Invalid model output (unparseable JSON, schema violation, refusal) is not retried or repaired: it is recorded as an invalid response and terminates the episode as unsolved. A valid direction that is visibly blocked is not retried or repaired: it is executed as a blocked move, counts as a wall hit, consumes the turn, and the episode continues.

aiTransport.policy: Provider requests use the shared Vercel AI SDK transport with structured output. SDK retries are disabled; Echo Maze owns every retry, pacing delay, and attempt record.

identity.coordinateSystem: Walker-relative coordinates start at (0,0). A successful move right changes x by +1, left by -1, up by +1, down by -1. A blocked move changes nothing. The Walker never receives absolute maze rows/columns.
identity.hiddenStatePolicy: The prompt receives only the narrow observation DTO (open/blocked directions, corridor sightlines, per-visible-cell open directions and isExit flag, last action/result) plus the current run's conversation. No full maze, no exit coordinates, no seed, no optimal route, no unseen cells, and no spectator state may enter the prompt.

payload.notes: Start (0,0); moved right to (1,0). Initial corridor had left/right open, up/down blocked. Explore rightward.
At (1,0), moved down into a new junction. Previous path: (0,0) to (1,0). Continue exploring the downward branch; backtracking remains possible via up.
At (1,-1), with up and right open. The downward branch was entered from above; explore the visible right corridor before backtracking.
At (2,-1) after moving right. Corridor continues both directions; continue right to explore the unvisited branch.
Current estimate (3,-1); last two right moves reached (3,-1). Left returns through explored corridor, so explore the open upward branch. No exit visible yet.
At (3,0) after moving up from the rightward corridor. Continue upward through the open vertical passage; the next visible junction offers a left branch to explore later.
At (3,2), continuing upward along the vertical passage. The cell ahead at (3,3) has a left branch, which is the next unvisited route to explore.
At (3,3), the upward route ended and a left branch is available. Explore left; down is the known vertical path for backtracking.
At (2,3) after moving left from (3,3). Right returns to the explored junction; explore the unvisited upward route.
At (2,4) after moving up from (2,3). Up is blocked; down returns to the explored branch. Explore the open right corridor, which extends three cells and may lead to a new junction.
At (3,4) after moving right from (2,4). The corridor continues right through one cell to a junction with an upward branch; continue right to explore the unvisited route.
At (4,4) after moving right along the upper corridor. Left returns to explored cells; continue right to reach the visible junction with an upward branch.
At (5,4) after moving right. Right is blocked; left returns through the explored corridor. Explore the open upward branch, tracking any new junction or exit.
At (5,5) after moving up from (5,4). Up remains unexplored; left and down provide backtracking routes. Continue upward to investigate the new branch and search for the exit.
At (5,6) after moving up. Up and right are blocked; down returns to the explored branch. Explore the open left route for a new passage or exit.
At (4,6) after moving left from (5,6). The corridor continues left and right; right returns to the explored branch. Continue left to explore the unvisited route and search for the exit.
At (3,6) after moving left from (4,6). Right leads back through the explored corridor; continue left to investigate the unvisited branch and search for the exit.
At (3,6); the attempted left move was blocked. Only right is open, so backtrack right toward the explored corridor and seek another unvisited branch.
At (4,6) after returning right from the blocked endpoint at (3,6). The left branch is exhausted; continue right toward (5,6), then investigate any remaining branch from the explored junction.
At (4,6); the left endpoint is exhausted. Return right to (5,6), then backtrack down toward (5,5) to investigate its remaining left branch.
At (5,6); right is blocked and left branch is exhausted. Move down to (5,5), then explore its unvisited left branch.
At (5,5) after moving down from (5,6). The left branch remains unexplored; investigate it now. Up and down are available for backtracking if needed.
At (4,5) after entering the previously unexplored left branch from (5,5). Continue left through the visible corridor to investigate its endpoint and search for the exit.
At (4,5), continued left along the newly explored branch. The next cell to the left is a junction with an upward route, so explore left first and then investigate upward.
At estimated (2,5) after moving left. The right corridor is known; explore the newly available upward branch first, while retaining down as the return route.
At (2,6) after moving up. Up and right are blocked; down returns to the explored branch. Explore the open left route for an unvisited passage or the exit.
At (1,6) after moving left from (2,6). Left and up are blocked. Right returns to the explored branch; explore the open downward route, which leads to a new junction.
At (1,5) after moving down from (1,6). The downward route is newly explored and leads to a cell with an available left branch; continue downward first to investigate it.
At (1,5) after moving down. Up returns to the known branch; the open left route is newly unexplored and should be investigated for the exit.

At estimated (0,5) after moving left from the previously explored branch. Both up and right are open; take the upward route first to continue systematic exploration, keeping right as the return branch.
At the new cell after moving up from (0,6). Up continues into an unexplored branch, while down backtracks to the known route. Continue upward systematically.
At the current junction after moving up; up and right are blocked. Down is the known return path, while left extends three cells and remains the best unexplored route. Continue left.
At (-2,5) after moving left from (-1,5). The corridor extends two cells left to an endpoint while right backtracks through the known route. Continue left to explore the remaining branch.
At the current corridor, left remains the unexplored direction and extends toward another junction or endpoint. Continue left; right is the backtracking route.
Moved left into a dead-end corridor segment; only right is open, so backtrack right toward the explored junction and continue searching for remaining branches.
At the corridor after backtracking right from the dead end. Continue right toward the junction and search for any remaining unexplored branch; left leads back to the exhausted endpoint.
At (-1,5) after backtracking right from the left dead end. Continue right through the known corridor toward the junction; investigate any branch encountered.
At (1,5). The right move succeeded; current junction has down and left open, with both routes extending. Left leads back through the explored corridor, so explore down for an unvisited branch.
At the vertical corridor after moving down. Continue downward through the open passage to explore the remaining branch; upward is the immediate backtracking route.
At the current cell after the successful down move. Up is the known return route; right is a newly available branch. Explore right before backtracking.
At (1,3) after the successful right move. Both up and left are known routes, but the cell above has an unexplored right branch noted earlier. Move up to reach that junction, then investigate right.
At the vertical corridor after moving up. Up leads to the visible junction with a right branch; investigate that unexplored route before backtracking down.
At the junction reached by moving up. Right is the newly identified branch to investigate; down is the known return route. Continue right systematically.

At the new cell after moving right from the junction. Up and right are blocked; both down and left are available. Explore down first as the likely unvisited branch, keeping left as an alternate route.
At (2,5) after moving down. Up leads to a dead-end cell, while right opens a three-cell corridor ending at a new junction. Explore right for the next unvisited branch.

At (3,5) after moving right. The corridor continues right through two cells, while left backtracks through the recently explored route. Continue right to reach the next junction and investigate its branches.
At (4,5) after moving right. The corridor continues left and right; the cell to the right is a junction with unexplored up and down branches. Continue right to investigate it.
At the rightmost junction after moving right. Right is blocked; left is the explored corridor, while up and down are available. Explore up first as the next unvisited branch.
At (5,6) after moving up from (5,5). The left branch has been explored to a dead end; move down to (5,5) and continue systematic backtracking through remaining junctions.
At (5,5), the upper branch was explored and the left branch led to an exhausted dead end. The downward route remains unexplored beyond the visible junction; descend to investigate it.
At (5,4) after descending from the main junction. Continue down into the remaining unexplored branch; the visible next cell offers up and left, while up returns to the explored junction.
Down was blocked, confirming the current cell is at the lower edge of this branch. Up is explored; move left through the corridor to continue searching for any unvisited junction or the exit.
At the corridor after moving left from the lower branch. Continue left toward the visible junction; this route remains the best unexplored direction, with right available for backtracking.
Moved left from the lower branch into the corridor. Continue left toward the junction and investigate the remaining route; right is available for backtracking.
At (2,4) after moving left. The right corridor is explored; up and left are blocked. Explore the open down branch, keeping right as the return route.
Moved down from the corridor at (2,4) into a junction with up and right open. The downward route is blocked; continue right to investigate the alternate branch while retaining up for backtracking.
At (3,3) after moving right. Both left and down lead through explored corridors; continue down to backtrack toward remaining unvisited branches and search for the exit.

At (3,2), both vertical directions are known, but the lower corridor leads toward the earlier junction at (3,0), whose left branch remains the best candidate for unvisited exploration. Descend toward it.
Descended to the vertical corridor near the earlier right-side junction. Continue down to reach the junction at the corridor’s lower end, then investigate its remaining left branch.
At (3,0); the unexplored left branch is open while up returns through the extensively explored vertical route. Move left to investigate this remaining corridor for the exit.

At the corridor after moving left from the right-side junction. Both left and right are open; the right route is explored, while the left cell has an upward branch. Continue left to investigate this remaining route for the exit.
At the newly reached left-side corridor cell after two left moves from the right junction. Right is explored; investigate the open upward branch, keeping right as the return route.
At (0,1) after moving up from the left-side corridor. Down returns to the explored route, while left extends through a previously unvisited corridor. Explore left for the exit.
At (-1,1) after moving left into the remaining unexplored corridor. Continue left toward the visible branch; right is the known return route, and the left cell may lead toward the exit.

At the newly reached branch after moving left. Right returns through the explored corridor; down is the remaining unexplored direction. Follow down to continue systematic exploration and search for the exit.
At (-2,0) after moving down from the branch. Up returns to the explored corridor; left remains unexplored and extends toward a junction. Continue left to search for the exit.
At (-3,0) after moving left from (-2,0). The corridor continues left to a junction with up, right, and down branches; continue left to investigate the remaining route for the exit.
At (-3,0), left is blocked and right is explored. The junction offers unexplored up and down branches; take up first and keep down as the next backtracking option.

At (-3,1) after moving up from the junction. The vertical passage continues upward for two cells, while down is the known return route. Continue up to reach the next junction and investigate its unexplored branches.

At (-3,3) after continuing up the unexplored vertical passage. Up remains open for one more cell toward a junction; down is the known return route. Continue upward to investigate the remaining branch.
At (-3,4) after moving up from the vertical passage. Up and left are blocked; down is the known return route, while right opens a new corridor. Explore right for an unvisited branch or the exit.

At (-2,4) after moving right from the vertical branch. The corridor continues both directions; left returns to the explored passage, while right reaches a junction with up, down, and left branches. Continue right to investigate it.
At (-1,4) after moving right into a junction. Left returns to the explored vertical passage; up and down are unexplored branches. Explore up first, keeping down as the next backtracking route.
At (-1,5) after moving up from the junction. Up is blocked; down returns to the known route, while left is the unexplored branch. Continue left to investigate it for the exit.
At (-2,5) after moving left from the junction. The left cell is newly explored and continues toward an upward branch; proceed left to investigate it, keeping right as the return route.
At (-2,5); continue left into the remaining unexplored corridor. Right remains the backtracking route.
Left is blocked, confirming the current cell is the corridor endpoint. Move up through the open branch to continue exploration; right remains the backtracking route.
At the endpoint branch after moving up from (-2,5). Up and left are blocked; right is an unexplored corridor extending two cells, while down is available for backtracking. Explore right first.

At (-1,6) after moving right from the branch endpoint. The corridor continues right to one more cell, while left backtracks and down is blocked. Continue right to inspect the remaining route for the exit.
At the endpoint reached by moving right. Only left is open, so backtrack left through the remaining corridor and continue systematic exploration.
Returned from the dead-end at (0,6) to (-1,6). Move left to (-2,6), then investigate its still-unexplored downward branch.
At (-2,6) after moving left from (-1,6). Right returns through the explored corridor; down is the remaining unexplored branch. Explore down for the exit.
At the cell reached after descending from the left-side branch. Down and left are blocked; up is a known return route, while right is the remaining unexplored direction. Explore right for the exit.
At the corridor after moving right from the left-side branch. Continue right into the newly explored cell; the left route is known for backtracking, while the right branch may lead toward the exit.
At the endpoint reached by moving right. Both left and down lead through previously explored corridors; descend to backtrack through the remaining central route and continue searching for the exit.

At the central junction after descending from the prior corridor. Up and left are explored routes; right is blocked. Continue down into the remaining branch, using the visible junction ahead to search for the exit.
At the junction after moving down. Down is blocked; the upward route is known. Explore the open right corridor first, while retaining left as a possible backtracking or alternate branch.
Moved right into a horizontal corridor. Up and down are blocked; continue right through the unexplored corridor, keeping left as the backtracking route.
At the current junction after moving right. Up and left are known routes, while right continues through an unexplored corridor toward a junction. Continue right to investigate for the exit.

At the rightmost junction after moving right. Right and up are blocked; left is the explored return corridor, while down leads to a new cell with an upward connection. Explore down before backtracking.
At (5,1) after moving down from the rightmost junction. Only up is open; move upward to continue through this narrow branch and investigate for the exit.
Returned up from the narrow dead-end to the junction at (5,2). The downward branch is exhausted; move left through the long corridor to continue systematic exploration and search for the exit.

At (4,2) after moving left from the rightmost junction. Up and right appear to lead through known routes; continue left along the remaining corridor to investigate its branches and search for the exit.
At the corridor after moving left from the right-side branch. Both directions are open; continue left into the remaining corridor to investigate the visible junction and search for the exit.

At the corridor after moving left from the right-side branch. The current cell has up, right, and left open; right returns through explored territory. Continue left toward the visible junction to investigate the remaining branch and search for the exit.

At (2,2), left leads to the remaining corridor and appears unvisited. Right is explored, down is blocked, and the upward route has already been investigated. Move left to continue systematic exploration.
At estimated (1,2); the attempted left move was blocked, so position is unchanged. Right is explored, while down leads to the remaining branch. Explore down next.
Moved down into a dead-end cell with only up open. Backtrack upward to the previous junction and continue exploring remaining branches.
At (1,1) after backtracking up from the dead-end below. Down is exhausted; right is the remaining corridor toward previously noted junctions and any unvisited branch. Proceed right.

At (2,1) after moving right from the junction. Up, right, and left are open; down is blocked. The right corridor is the remaining unexplored route, so continue right while tracking for a new junction or exit.

At (2,1) after moving right. The corridor continues right through previously less-explored cells; up and left are known routes, while right is the best remaining direction to investigate for the exit.
At (4,1) after moving right. The corridor continues right to a cell with a downward branch; up and down are blocked here. Continue right to investigate the remaining route for the exit.

At the rightmost junction after moving right. The downward cell is a known dead end, and the remaining route is left through the long corridor. Backtrack left to continue searching for any unvisited branch or the exit.
Returned left from the right-side dead end to the junction at (4,1). The right route is exhausted; explore the open upward branch, keeping left as the backtracking route.
At (4,2) after moving up from the right-side junction. Up and right are blocked; down returns to the explored branch, while left is the remaining route to investigate for the exit.
At the endpoint reached by moving left from the right-side branch. Only right is open, so backtrack right through the explored corridor and continue searching for any remaining branch or exit.
At (4,2) after moving right from the left endpoint. Left returns to the exhausted endpoint; down is the explored corridor toward the remaining central junctions. Backtrack down systematically.
At (4,1) after moving down. The right branch and upper route are explored; left remains the best direction toward the central corridor and any unvisited branch or exit.

At (3,1) after moving left from the right-side corridor. The corridor continues left toward a junction and a further branch; right is the explored return route. Continue left to investigate the remaining route for the exit.
At (2,1) after returning from the right-side corridor. Right has been exhausted; the upward route is explored, so move left through the central corridor to continue searching for the exit.

At the current junction after moving left. Left and up are blocked; the downward branch is a known dead end from prior exploration. Move right through the corridor to continue searching remaining routes for the exit.
At the central junction after moving right. Right and left corridors are extensively explored; move up through the open branch to continue systematic coverage and search for the exit.

Moved up from the central junction to (2,3). The current cell has up, down, and left open; down returns to explored corridors, while up is the most promising remaining branch. Continue upward to investigate for the exit.
At (2,4) after moving up. Up and right are blocked; down returns to explored corridors, while left is open and remains the best unexplored route. Move left to continue searching for the exit.

At (1,4) after moving left from the upper central corridor. Both left and right are open; right returns to the explored junction, while left continues toward the remaining branch. Continue left to investigate for the exit.
Moved left from the upper central corridor to the current junction, estimated at (0,4). Right returns through explored territory; take the open upward branch to continue searching for the exit.
After moving up, the current cell has right and down open, with up and left blocked. Down is the known return route; explore right through the visible corridor for the remaining route or exit.

At (0,6) after backtracking from the right dead end. The right branch is exhausted; move down along the remaining open route to continue systematic exploration.
At (0,5) after moving down from the dead-end branch. Up returns to the explored loop; move right toward the central corridor to continue searching for any remaining branch or the exit.
